ONLY AS CLAIMED BY THE APPELLANT BEFORE THIS COURT AND ORDER FOR COSTS OF THIS APPEAL.
 THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR FURTHER ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This appeal is by the injured claimant aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 15.02.2018 passed in MVC No.1291/2015 on the file of I Addl.

Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi (for short 'Tribunal'), by which, the NC: 2023:KHC-K:9342 claim petition of the claimant has been partly allowed by granting compensation of Rs.14,32,000/- with interest at 6% per annum from the Imran @ Shaikh Imran S/O Shaikh Nabi vs Sri Shant Reddy And Ors on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174349657/
2 date of petition till realisation, directing respondent No.2 - Insurance Company to pay the compensation.
2.

entities.text: Shaikh Nabi vs Sri Shant Reddy And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Brief facts of the case are that, on 25.09.2015, the claimant was proceeding on a motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-29/R-6535 along with one Fayaz.

At about 7.30 p.m., when they were near Halakatta Darga main gate, a Tractor-Trailer bearing Reg.No.KA-32/TA-5177/5178 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, dashed the motorcycle of the claimant, in which he sustained grievous injuries to his head, left eye, nose, hands, legs, chin and other parts of the body.
The claimant was treated as an inpatient between 25.09.2015 and 02.11.2015.

Thereupon, he filed a claim petition, seeking compensation of Rs.43,78,000/- on the premise that he was aged 21 years,
working as a coolie in stone quarry and earning Rs.700/- per day.

That, since he was NC:
2023:KHC-K:9342 a skilled labourer, he was earning more wages and due to the accident, he has sustained disability not being able to do any sort of work as he was doing earlier.

3. Objection statements were filed by respondent No.2-Insurance Company, denying the petition averments and contending that the accident has taken place on account of the rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle.
It was also contended that the driver of the tractor-trailer did not have valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Hence, sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
4. The Tribunal on consideration of the pleadings, framed issues and recorded the evidence.
On behalf of the claimant, his father has been examined as PW.1 and Dr.Santosh J. Mangshetty, a Neuro Surgeon, who treated the claimant has been examined as PW.2.
15 documents have been marked as Exs.P1 to P15.

No evidence has been adduced on behalf of the respondents except marking copy of the insurance policy as Ex.R1.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:9342 5.

The Tribunal, on appreciation of the evidence has held that the accident in question has occurred on account of rash and negligent driving of the tractor-trailer by its driver and consequently held that the claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.14,32,000/- with interest at 6% per annum and directed respondent No.2- Insurance Company to pay the entire compensation.
Being aggrieved by the same, the claimant is before this Court.

6. Sri Sanjeev Patil, learned counsel appearing for the appellant reiterating the grounds urged in the memorandum of appeal submits that PW.2, who is a treated doctor has assessed the disability at 40%.
However, the Tribunal has reduced it to 35%.
He submits that the appellant was earning Rs.700/- per day being a skilled labourer, apart from earning Bhatta.
But, the Tribunal has assessed the income at Rs.7,500/- per month.

He further submits that the grant of compensation NC:
2023:KHC-K:9342 on other heads is also on the lower side and seeks for enhancement.

7. On the other hand, Sri Uday P. Honguntikar, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 - Insurance Company submits that the assessment of disability at 35% by the Tribunal is just and proper, so also the grant of compensation on other heads, warranting no interference.

Hence, seeks Imran @ Shaikh Imran S/O Shaikh Nabi vs Sri Shant Reddy And Ors on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174349657/
3 for dismissal of the appeal.

8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the records.
9.
The accident in question resulting in grievous injuries to the appellant is not in dispute.
10. It is seen that the appellant not being in a position to depose, his father has been examined as a witness.
PW.2, the treating doctor in his evidence has deposed regarding the injuries, diagnosis and the treatment that was given to the petitioner.

As per Ex.P7 - Wound Certificate, the appellant has sustained the following injuries:
"Peri orbital edema on both eyes.
CLW over frontal scalp.
CLW over left knee front.
Comminuted fracture of frontal bone.
Sub dural hemorrhage on right frontal region."

12. As per the Disability Certificate - Ex.P10, PW.2, the treated doctor has opined as under:
"Mr. Shaik Imran S/o Mr. Shaik Nabi aged about 23 years was admitted in Vaatsalya Life Hospital Kalaburagi with alleged history of RTA on 25/09/2015.
He was diagnosed to have comminuted fracture of frontal bone with subdural hemorrhage in frontal region.
He underwent left fronto temporo parietal decompressive craniectomy and SDH evacuation in September 2015 and later on in November 2015 cramioplasty was done.
Post operatively he has been under my regular follow up and during this period he had multiple episodes of seizures (fits).
He has impaired higher mental function and is prove for seizure in his future life also.
He may not be able to perform heavy labour work in future (as titanium mesh is placed in skull bone defect).
Currently he is taking medicines amounting to about Rs.2,000/- per month.

On 22/8/2017 after performing Neurobehavioural and Cognitive Assessment using (1) Motor speed (2) verbal fluency (3) category fluency (4) verbal working memory (5) planning (6) set shifting (7) verbal comprehension (8) verbal learning & memory (9) perceptual Gestalt and (10) NC: 2023:KHC-K:9342 focal signs, based on NIMHANS Neuropsychological Battery 2004 (Head Injury), I am of the opinion that the Neurological Disabilities amounts to about 40% (forty percent only)."
13.
The doctor has assessed the disability at 40%.
Further, perusal of the photographs made available on record would also indicate the severity of the injuries sustained by the appellant.

Considering the nature of avocation being carried on by the appellant who is skilled labourer in the stone quarry and the injuries sustained by him, the assessment of disability at 40% made by the treated doctor cannot be interference with.
The Tribunal having appreciated the evidence has reduced the disability to 35%, however, there is no justifiable reason for reducing the same in the absence of any cogent evidence in this regard.
Even in the cross-examination of PW.2, nothing has been brought on record to discredit the deposition of the doctor.
On the other hand, in the cross- examination, PW.2 has further clarified the nature of injuries and the treatment provided to the appellant.
The doctor has specifically deposed that though physically NC: 2023:KHC-K:9342 claimant appears to be able, since he has suffered injuries to his brain, he has lost the earning capability.

The doctor has also stated that since the claimant has sustained injuries to the brain,
there is no possibility of he recovering from the injuries.
In that view of the matter, 40% of disability assessed by the doctor is sustained.

14. As regards the income of the appellant is concerned, though it was claimed that he was earning Rs.700/- per day and in addition he was also earning substantial sum of bhatta, no document has been produced to substantiate the same.
The Tribunal has assessed the income at Rs.7,500/- per month.

As per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, the notional income in respect of the victims of the road traffic accident of the year 2015 is assessed at Rs.8,000/- per month.
The same is taken in this case as well.

15. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Erudaya Priya vs. State Express Transport Corporation - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:9342 Limited reported in AIR 2020 Supreme Court 4284 has held that even in injury cases, claimant would be entitled for addition of future prospects.

entities.text: Erudaya Priya vs. State Express Transport Corporation - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:9342 Limited reported in AIR 2020 Supreme Court 4284
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since disability sustained by the appellant is substantial and considering age of appellant as 21 years, it would be appropriate to add 40% towards future prospects.
Considering the age of the appellant, multiplier of '18' is applied.
16. Thus, calculated as above, the appellant would be entitled for a sum of Rs.9,67,680/- (Rs.8,000 + 40% x 12 x 18 x 40%) towards loss of future earning.
17. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards pain and suffering.
The same is enhanced to Rs.75,000/- by adding Rs.45,000/-.
18. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards attendant, conveyance charges and nutrition of food etc.

Since the appellant was admitted as an inpatient from 25.09.2015 to 02.11.2015 i.e., for about 40 days, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on lesser - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:9342 side and the same is enhanced to Rs.50,000/- by adding Rs.30,000/-.

5 19. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.7,15,000/- towards medical expenses and Rs.1,00,000/-
towards future medical expenses.
The same is maintained as it is.
20. The Tribunal has not awarded any compensation towards loss of income during laid up period.
Considering nature of injuries sustained by appellant, he might have been advised rest for about three months.

Therefore, loss of income during laid up period is to be Rs.24,000/- (Rs.8,000 x 3).
21.
The Tribunal has not awarded any compensation towards loss of amenities.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the appellant, this Court is of the considered view that a sum of Rs.50,000/- be awarded under the said head.

Thus, the appellant is held entitled for a total compensation of Rs.19,81,680/- instead of Rs.14,32,000/- awarded by the Tribunal as under:
